Finding: SHIPPED CONTENT INSIDE AN HTML COMMENT - THREE TIMES IN ONE DAY, AND ONE OF THEM WAS COMMITTED AND PUSHED THAT WAY. SCRATCH.md opens with a TEMPLATE block, inside `<!-- -->`, that lists the section headings verbatim. Every scripted insert this session anchored on a heading string ('## NEXT SESSION (dated, priority-ordered)', '## OPEN THREADS') and Python's str.replace(...,1) hit the FIRST occurrence - which is the one INSIDE THE COMMENT. GENERAL FORM: a template or example block that quotes its own real section headings makes every heading-anchored edit AMBIGUOUS, and the failure is SILENT because the content is present in the file, passes every schema/lint/claim_check, greps positive, and renders as nothing. FIXES, in order of strength: (1) anchor on the LAST occurrence, or on a body-unique string, never the first; (2) after any scripted insert, verify placement by heading OFFSET (which occurrence) rather than by presence; (3) best - do not let a template block quote live heading text verbatim. Finding: COMMENT-SHADOWING BUG FIXED AT SOURCE, AND THE FIX IS THE STRONGEST OF THE THREE AVAILABLE. ML-RED-155 recorded the defect: SCRATCH.md's TEMPLATE block quoted its own live section headings verbatim ('## OPEN THREADS' etc.), so every heading-anchored scripted edit matched the COMMENTED copy first and wrote content inside `<!-- -->`. THREE FIXES WERE AVAILABLE, ranked weakest to strongest: (1) anchor on the LAST occurrence - fixes the caller, not the file, and every future caller has to remember; (2) verify placement by heading OFFSET after each insert - a check, so it only fires if someone runs it; (3) REMOVE THE AMBIGUITY - stop the template quoting live heading text. Took (3): the template now lists section names as a numbered list WITHOUT the '##' prefix, carries an explicit 'DO NOT restore the ## prefixes' warning with the incident and commit hash, and states the anchor-on-a-body-unique-string rule for future scripted edits. *** VERIFIED FUNCTIONALLY, NOT BY INSPECTION: *** each of the six body headings now matches exactly once (was twice), and a simulated naive first-occurrence insert - the exact failure mode - was confirmed to land in the BODY, not the comment. GENERAL FORM WORTH CARRYING: when a file contains an EXAMPLE of its own structure, the example is indistinguishable from the structure to every string-matching tool. Prefer removing the ambiguity over adding a check that detects it - a check that must be remembered is the same class of failure as the bug.

Finding: csv.reader SILENTLY MANGLED A TSV THAT CONTAINS LITERAL QUOTE CHARACTERS, AND THE WRITE-BACK PERSISTED THE MANGLED PARSE. Python's csv module defaults to quotechar='"' with doublequote=True, so a TSV cell whose content merely CONTAINS or STARTS WITH a double-quote is parsed as a quoted field: the quotes are consumed and the content re-interpreted. A read-modify-write round-trip then writes the parsed value back as truth. Live instance: PREDICTIONS.tsv row RED-08's Outcome cell went from '"' to 'W' in a pass whose only intended edit was one Status value on a DIFFERENT row - and the corruption showed up as 6 changed rows where 1 was intended. Detected by reading the diff rather than the exit code, restored via git checkout (uncommitted), and redone with raw line splitting.
Data_Quote: Quote-character counts in RED workbook TSVs: ML.tsv 36, CHALLENGES.tsv 10, KB.tsv 6, PREDICTIONS.tsv 6. Registry FALSIFICATION_TRIGGERS.tsv = 0, which is the only reason two earlier csv round-trips on it this session were safe - verified field-by-field against a pre-change backup, 0 unintended changes.
Thesis_Impact: None - caught pre-commit. The near-miss is that the SAME method had already been used twice on the falsification registry hours earlier and survived ONLY because that file happens to contain no quote characters.
Notes: FOURTH member of the one-family tooling class and the most dangerous, because it corrupts SILENTLY AND SELECTIVELY - it does not raise, does not truncate, and touches only the rows that happen to contain a quote. RULE: do NOT use the csv module on these TSVs at all; split on tab, join on tab. The generalisable tell is a diff LARGER THAN THE EDIT - 6 rows changed for a 1-row edit is a corruption signature, and the only reason it was caught is that the row count was checked against intent. VERIFY THE DIFF SIZE MATCHES THE INTENDED EDIT COUNT.
